query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:

query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **[UserLM-R1: Modeling Human Reasoning in User Language Models with Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09215)** (2026). A close match: adaptive user profiles, strategic decision-making, and rewards for consistency, reasoning quality, and resistance to manipulation. **People:** Feng Zhang, Shijia Li, Chunmao Zhang, Zhanyu Ma, Jun Xu, Jiuchong Gao, Jinghua Hao, Renqing He, Jingwen Xu, and Han Liu. **Affiliations:** Meituan, Peking University, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Dalian University of Technology.

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)**. Studies how turn-level rewards and conversation-level scoring affect LLM agents trained against simulated users. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (**University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign**); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (**Salesforce AI Research**).

3. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336)** (2026). Trains simulators using an LLM judge’s assessment of whether responses are indistinguishable from a real user’s, conditioned on user history. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations:** MIT, Stanford University, and MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab.

4. **[What does it take to build a human-like user simulator?](https://nickatomlin.github.io/blog/user-simulators-2.html)** (2025). A useful conceptual overview of simulator context, interaction scaffolds, and training objectives—including incentives reflecting user effort, attention, and preferences. **People:** Nicholas Tomlin (**Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago**, currently) and Jessy Lin (**UC Berkeley / Berkeley AI Research**, per her [research profile](https://jessylin.com/)).

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[Learning to Learn-at-Test-Time: Language Agents with Learnable Adaptation Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.00830)** (2026). Closest match: Meta-TTL learns an adaptation strategy across training tasks, then uses it to improve an agent over repeated test-time episodes. **People:** Zhanzhi Lou, Hui Chen, Yibo Li, Qian Wang, and Bryan Hooi — National University of Singapore.

2. **[Environments as Scaffold: Enriching Feedback to Bootstrap Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08404)** (2026). Studies how feedback should change during both within-episode exploration and across-episode RL training. **People:** Hongbang Yuan — Fudan University; Zhuoran Jin — CASIA; Yixin Cao — Fudan University and Shanghai Innovation Institute.

3. **[CLIN: A Continually Learning Language Agent for Rapid Task Adaptation and Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10134)** (2023). Uses persistent textual memory to improve across repeated trials and transfer experience to new tasks and environments, without updating model weights. **People:** Bodhisattwa Prasad Majumder, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Oyvind Tafjord, Niket Tandon, and Peter Clark — Allen Institute for AI; Peter Jansen — University of Arizona; Li Zhang and Chris Callison-Burch — University of Pennsylvania.

4. **[Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13417)** (2026). Evaluation-focused: measures within-run feedback handling and whether experience improves subsequent attempts or different tasks. **People:** Yiwei Li and colleagues — Meituan; Wanli Yang, Hexiang Tan, and Fei Sun — University of Chinese Academy of Sciences.

1. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19682)** — December 2025. Trains agents alongside a simulator that generates tasks matched to their evolving capabilities. **People:** Jiacheng Guo, Jiahao Qiu, and Mengdi Wang (Princeton); Ling Yang (Princeton and ByteDance Seed); Ke Shen (ByteDance Seed); Peter Chen (Columbia); Qixin Xiao and Xinzhe Juan (University of Michigan); Yinjie Wang (University of Chicago).

2. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24426)** — May 2026. Uses agent failures to jointly improve tool-use policies and the environment’s learning interface. **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, and Wei Wu. **Team affiliations:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, and University of Science and Technology of China.

3. **[CoEvolve: Training LLM Agents via Agent-Data Mutual Evolution](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.1055/)** — ACL, July 2026. 4. **[Co-Evolution in Agentic Systems: Toward Self-Directed Evolution Beyond Human Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.10299)** — August 2026. text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — Eight dialogue and text-game tasks, with offline datasets and online simulators for RL training and evaluation. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai, and Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind).

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** — Combines simulated users, multi-turn RL, and eight evaluation environments built on UserBench. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, and Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

3. **[τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07982)** — Tests coordination between agents and simulated users who can both act through tools, including telecom troubleshooting. **People:** Victor Barres, Soham Ray, and Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra); Honghua Dong (Sierra, University of Toronto, and Vector Institute); Xujie Si (University of Toronto and Vector Institute).

4. **[SimulatorArena: Are User Simulators Reliable Proxies for Multi-Turn Evaluation of AI Assistants?](https://www.simulatorarena.ai/)** — Evaluates simulator fidelity against 909 human–LLM conversations in math tutoring and document creation; useful for validating the simulated users behind RL benchmarks. **People:** Yao Dou, Alan Ritter, and Wei Xu (Georgia Tech); Michel Galley, Baolin Peng, Chris Kedzie, Weixin Cai, Chris Quirk, and Jianfeng Gao (Microsoft).

5. **[MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18669v1)** — A related training framework incorporating simulated users into RL, evaluated on τ-bench, τ²-bench, BFCL, and ACEBench. **People:** Weikang Zhao (Meituan and Chinese Academy of Sciences); Xili Wang (Meituan and Peking University); Chengdi Ma (Peking University); Lingbin Kong, Zhaohua Yang, Mingxiang Tuo, Xiaowei Shi, Yitao Zhai, and Xunliang Cai (Meituan).

text:

2. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02208)** (2025). Introduces **UserVille**, preference-aware simulated users, and **PPP**, reinforcement learning that rewards task completion, useful clarification questions, and personalization. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang (Carnegie Mellon University), with Xingyao Wang (OpenHands).

3. **[MIMESIS: Learning User Simulators as Training Environments for Interactive Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09484)** (2026). Learns realistic user behavior from human conversations, then improves agents using reinforcement learning and coaching derived from simulator feedback. **People:** Hoang Phan (Meta Superintelligence Labs; New York University), Changdae Oh (Meta; University of Wisconsin–Madison), Dat Huynh, Qi Zeng, Wancen Mu, Yue Cao, Shengjie Bi, Yun He, Deren Lei (Meta), and Andrey Zhmoginov.
